```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Daud 2011 contributes two models:

* `Daud_2011_peginterferon_alfa_2b` -- the integrated PK/PD model: a
  one-compartment PK model for subcutaneous peginterferon alfa-2b driving an
  indirect-response model of the absolute neutrophil count (ANC).
* `Daud_2011_peginterferon_alfa_2b_anc_auc` -- the static inhibitory Imax
  model relating steady-state weekly AUCtau to the ANC change, fitted to
  dose-group means pooled with a solid-tumour study.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Daud_2011_peginterferon_alfa_2b"))$reference`
* Description (PK/PD): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Daud_2011_peginterferon_alfa_2b"))$description`
* Description (AUC Imax): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Daud_2011_peginterferon_alfa_2b_anc_auc"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-010-1326-9> (open access:
  <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3043235/>)

The parameter values and the PD equations are in the article's electronic
supplementary material (supplementary Methods, supplementary Table 1).

# Population

Thirty-two adults with completely resected AJCC stage IIB-IIIC melanoma were
enrolled in a phase II, open-label, single-arm PK study at four sites
(NCT00457418). They received peginterferon alfa-2b 6 ug/kg SC once weekly for
8 weeks (induction) and then 3 ug/kg once weekly (maintenance); the first 12
weeks formed the PK phase. Age was 20-77 years (median 50), weight 46-137 kg
(median 82), 31% were female and 97% White (Daud 2011 Table 1). The
noncompartmental analysis (Table 3) used the 20 patients who received full
doses and gave every PK sample; the compartmental PK parameters are geometric
means over 32 individual fits and the ANC PD parameters over 31.

The Imax exposure-response model additionally pooled dose-group means from 34
patients with advanced solid tumours treated with 0.75-7.5 ug/kg/week
(Bukowski 2002), six of whom had melanoma.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Daud_2011_peginterferon_alfa_2b")()$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| One-compartment PK, first-order absorption and elimination, no lag | -- | Supplementary Methods, Scheme 1 |
| `lka` (K01) | log(0.161) 1/h | Supplementary Table 1 (CV 83%) |
| `lkel` (K10) | log(0.0137) 1/h | Supplementary Table 1 (CV 35%) |
| `lvc` (V/F) | log(1.08) L/kg | Supplementary Table 1 (CV 38%) |
| V/F scaled linearly by `WT` | exponent 1 | per-kg reporting of V/F and per-kg dosing (Methods, Treatment) |
| dR/dt = Kin [1 - Cp/(Cp + IC50)] - Kout R | -- | Supplementary Table 1, ANC equation; Supplementary Methods, Scheme 2 |
| `lkin` (Kin) | log(57.9) per day | Supplementary Table 1, ANC PK/PD (CV 145%) |
| `lkout` (Kout) | log(0.526) 1/day | Supplementary Table 1, ANC PK/PD (CV 150%) |
| `lic50` (IC50) | log(453) pg/mL | Supplementary Table 1, ANC PK/PD (CV 84%) |
| `eta*` variances | log(1 + CV^2) | Supplementary Table 1 %CV columns |
| `propSd`, `addSd_ANC` | fixed(0) | not reported |
| E = E0 - (E0 - Imax) AUC / (IC50 + AUC) | -- | Supplementary Methods (printed form differs; see Assumptions) and Fig. 2 |
| `lrbase` (E0) | log(98.7) % | Supplementary Table 1, Imax model |
| `limax` (Imax) | log(33.3) % | Supplementary Table 1, Imax model |
| `lauc50` (IC50 on AUCtau) | log(80900) pg*h/mL | Supplementary Table 1, Imax model |

# Dosing regimen

The protocol regimen is 6 ug/kg weekly for 8 doses and then 3 ug/kg weekly.
Because both the dose and V/F scale with body weight, the typical
concentration and ANC profiles do not depend on weight.

```{r regimen}
mod <- readModelDb("Daud_2011_peginterferon_alfa_2b")
tau <- 168

make_events <- function(id, wt, maint_dose, obs_times) {
  dose_times <- (0:11) * tau
  dose_ugkg <- c(rep(6, 8), rep(maint_dose, 4))
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = dose_times, amt = dose_ugkg * wt, evid = 1L,
    cmt = "depot", WT = wt
  )
  doses <- doses[doses$amt > 0, ]
  # The model declares two endpoints (Cc and ANC); observation rows name the
  # ODE state and carry dvid so rxode2 maps them onto the endpoint slots.
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L,
    WT = wt
  )
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |> dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
```

# PK: typical profile (Figure 1)

```{r fig1, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
ev_typ <- make_events(1L, 82, 3, seq(0, 12 * tau, by = 1))
sim_typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ))

# Published means (Table 3 and Results text): Cmax at 24 h post-dose in
# weeks 1, 8 and 12, and predose troughs in weeks 8, 10, 11 and 12.
obs_pub <- data.frame(
  time = c(24, 7 * tau + 24, 11 * tau + 24, 7 * tau, 9 * tau, 10 * tau, 11 * tau),
  conc = c(3980, 5070, 2620, 1300, 684, 526, 626),
  what = c(rep("Cmax (Table 3)", 3), rep("Trough (Table 3 / text)", 4))
)

ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time / tau + 1, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = obs_pub, aes(time / tau + 1, conc, shape = what)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (week)", y = "Serum peginterferon alfa-2b (pg/mL)", shape = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Daud 2011 (typical-value curve with published mean values)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# PK: noncompartmental comparison (Table 3)

A virtual cohort of 200 patients (weights drawn from the Table 1 mean and SD,
truncated to the observed range) is simulated with the reported
between-patient variability and sampled at the study's nominal times (predose,
24, 48, 96 and 168 h in weeks 1, 8 and 12). NCA follows the paper: AUC over
the 168 h interval, Cmax, Cavg, Cmin and Tmax.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20110301)
n_sub <- 200
wt <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 84, 21), 46), 137)
week_start <- c(`1` = 0, `8` = 7 * tau, `12` = 11 * tau)
obs_times <- sort(unique(as.vector(outer(c(0, 24, 48, 96, 168), week_start, "+"))))
ev_pop <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
  make_events(i, wt[i], 3, obs_times)
}))
sim_pop <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_pop, returnType = "data.frame"))
```

```{r nca}
conc_df <- sim_pop |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc) |>
  dplyr::cross_join(data.frame(week = names(week_start), start = week_start)) |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= start, time <= start + tau) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - start, treatment = paste("Week", week)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, tad, Cc)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ tad | treatment + id)
dose_df <- conc_df |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    tad = 0,
    dose = ifelse(treatment == "Week 12", 3, 6)
  )
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ tad | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = tau, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cav = TRUE,
  cmin = TRUE, tmax = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res)

# Table 3 reports arithmetic means (median for Tmax), so summarise the same way.
sim_sum <- nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "cav", "cmin", "tmax")) |>
  # Table 3 gives no week-1 trough (the predose sample is before any dose).
  dplyr::filter(!(PPTESTCD == "cmin" & treatment == "Week 1")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    PPORRES = ifelse(PPTESTCD[1] == "tmax", median(PPORRES), mean(PPORRES)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ref <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("Week 1", "Week 8", "Week 12"),
  auclast = c(324000, 462000, 235000),
  cmax = c(3980, 5070, 2620),
  cav = c(1930, 2750, 1400),
  cmin = c(NA, 1300, 626),
  tmax = c(24, 24, 24)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_sum, ref,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "pg*h/mL", cmax = "pg/mL", cav = "pg/mL", cmin = "pg/mL", tmax = "h")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs Daud 2011 Table 3 (AUC0-tau labelled AUClast; 168 h interval).")
```

`r paste(attr(cmp, "footnote"), collapse = " ")`

```{r nca-check}
pct <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("%", "", sub("\\*$", "", cmp[["% diff"]]))))
is_trough <- grepl("^Cmin", cmp[["NCA parameter"]])
stopifnot(
  # Guard against a vacuous check if the table format changes.
  sum(!is.na(pct)) == 14,
  # AUC, Cmax and Cavg: a wrong unit, V/F or kel would move these by
  # multiples; the cohort means sit within 15% of Table 3.
  all(abs(pct[!is_trough]) < 25, na.rm = TRUE),
  # Troughs run about 20% low (see text); bound the structural error only.
  all(abs(pct[is_trough]) < 40, na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

The model reproduces the published AUC, Cmax and Cavg to within about 15%;
the simulated troughs are about 20% below the published means, which have the
largest between-patient CV in Table 3 (43-56%). Two other features of Table 3
are not reproduced exactly and are not expected to be: the PK parameters are
geometric means of individual fits while Table 3 is an arithmetic mean over a
20-patient subset, and the reported accumulation factor
R = 1.69 (the mean of individual week 8 / week 1 AUC ratios) is larger than
both the ratio of the mean AUCs (462,000 / 324,000 = 1.43) and the
accumulation implied by a 43-51 h half-life with weekly dosing (about 1.1).
The simulated mean ratio is shown below for reference.

```{r accumulation}
acc <- nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", treatment %in% c("Week 1", "Week 8")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(R = `Week 8` / `Week 1`)
data.frame(
  quantity = c("Mean individual R (simulated)", "R published (Table 3)",
               "Typical-value accumulation 1/(1 - exp(-kel * tau))"),
  value = c(mean(acc$R), 1.69, 1 / (1 - exp(-0.0137 * tau)))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# ANC: indirect response with dose modification (Figure 3a)

Figure 3a simulates the median ANC with 6 ug/kg/week for weeks 1-8 and then
3, 2, 1 or 0 ug/kg/week, or continued 6 ug/kg/week, for weeks 9-12. The
figure's x-axis labels the first dose as week 1.

```{r fig3a, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
scen <- c(6, 3, 2, 1, 0)
sim_anc <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(scen), function(i) {
  ev <- make_events(i, 82, scen[i], seq(0, 12 * tau, by = 2))
  out <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev))
  out$maintenance <- paste(scen[i], "ug/kg")
  out
}))
sim_anc$maintenance <- factor(sim_anc$maintenance, levels = paste(scen, "ug/kg"))

ggplot(sim_anc, aes(time / tau + 1, ANC, linetype = maintenance)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (week)", y = "ANC (% of baseline)", linetype = "Weeks 9-12 dose",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3a of Daud 2011 (typical values)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The paper reports that continued 6 ug/kg/week keeps the ANC at about 33% of
baseline (the level of weeks 2-8), and that reducing the weeks 9-12 dose to
3, 2 or 1 ug/kg/week increases the ANC by 13, 22 and 38%. The comparison is
made at the end of the simulated period (Figure 3a week 13).

```{r anc-check}
plateau <- sim_anc |>
  dplyr::filter(maintenance == "6 ug/kg", time >= tau, time <= 8 * tau) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean = mean(ANC), min = min(ANC), max = max(ANC))
end_anc <- sim_anc |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 12 * tau) |>
  dplyr::select(maintenance, ANC)
ref_6 <- end_anc$ANC[end_anc$maintenance == "6 ug/kg"]
end_anc <- end_anc |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    increase_vs_6 = ANC - ref_6,
    published_increase = c(NA, 13, 22, 38, NA)
  )
knitr::kable(plateau, digits = 1, caption = "Simulated ANC (% of baseline), weeks 2-8 at 6 ug/kg/week.")
knitr::kable(end_anc, digits = 1, caption = "ANC at Figure 3a week 13 by weeks 9-12 dose.")

stopifnot(
  # Deterministic typical-value solve.
  plateau$mean > 20, plateau$mean < 33,
  # The ANC rises monotonically as the maintenance dose falls.
  all(diff(end_anc$ANC) > 0),
  # Increases within 8 points of the published 13 / 22 / 38%.
  all(abs(end_anc$increase_vs_6[2:4] - c(13, 22, 38)) < 8)
)
```

During induction the simulated ANC oscillates between
`r round(plateau$min, 1)`% and `r round(plateau$max, 1)`% of baseline (mean
`r round(plateau$mean, 1)`%), as the published curve does between about 20%
and 33%; the "33% of baseline" quoted in the Results is the upper end of that
range and the level of the observed medians. The dose-reduction increases
follow the published 13, 22 and 38% but run 4-6 points higher, and the
reduced-dose and 0 ug/kg arms sit about 10% above Figure 3a, because the
model starts and recovers at R(0) = Kin/Kout =
57.9 / 0.526 = 110% of baseline, the ratio of the tabulated geometric means,
whereas the published curve starts at 100% and the 0 ug/kg arm returns to
about 99%. The figure was therefore drawn with a Kin/Kout close to 100,
which the tabulated geometric means do not give; the model keeps the
tabulated values.

# ANC: steady-state AUC Imax model (Figure 2)

```{r fig2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
mod_auc <- readModelDb("Daud_2011_peginterferon_alfa_2b_anc_auc")
auc_grid <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = seq(0, 700000, by = 5000), evid = 0L,
  AUC_PEGINTERFERON_ALFA_2B = seq(0, 700000, by = 5000)
)
auc_grid$time <- seq_len(nrow(auc_grid))
sim_auc <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_auc, auc_grid))
sim_auc$AUC <- auc_grid$AUC_PEGINTERFERON_ALFA_2B

# Dose-group means read approximately from Daud 2011 Fig. 2 by the maintainers
# (validation only; no parameter is derived from them).
fig2 <- data.frame(
  AUC = c(47000, 106000, 233000, 242000, 397000, 461000, 479000, 616000),
  ANC = c(76.5, 60.3, 48.6, 51.4, 49.7, 38.5, 40.2, 43.0),
  group = c("Solid tumour", "Solid tumour", "Melanoma", "Solid tumour",
            "Solid tumour", "Melanoma", "Solid tumour", "Solid tumour")
)
printed_form <- function(auc) 98.7 - 33.3 * auc / (80900 + auc)

ggplot(sim_auc, aes(AUC, ANC)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(aes(y = printed_form(AUC)), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(data = fig2, aes(shape = group)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 16)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 120)) +
  labs(
    x = "Mean AUCtau (pg*h/mL)", y = "ANC (% of baseline)", shape = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 2 of Daud 2011. Solid: packaged model;",
      "dashed: the equation as printed in the supplementary Methods."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig2-check}
pred_pkg <- 98.7 - (98.7 - 33.3) * fig2$AUC / (80900 + fig2$AUC)
rmse <- c(
  packaged = sqrt(mean((pred_pkg - fig2$ANC)^2)),
  printed = sqrt(mean((printed_form(fig2$AUC) - fig2$ANC)^2))
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(form = names(rmse), rmse = rmse), digits = 1,
             caption = "RMS deviation from the Fig. 2 dose-group means (percentage points).", row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(rmse[["packaged"]] < 6, rmse[["printed"]] > 3 * rmse[["packaged"]])
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Imax model form.** The supplementary Methods print the inhibitory model as
  E = E0 - Imax C / (IC50 + C). With the tabulated E0 = 98.7%, Imax = 33.3%
  and IC50 = 80,900 pg*h/mL that form cannot fall below 65% of baseline, yet
  the model-fit curve and the dose-group means in Figure 2 level off near
  40%. The form E = E0 - (E0 - Imax) AUC / (IC50 + AUC), in which Imax is the
  response at saturating exposure, reproduces Figure 2 with the same three
  values (table above), and agrees with the Results statement that ANC stays
  at about 33% of baseline at full dose. The packaged model uses that form.
* **Between-patient variability.** The parameters are geometric means of
  individual WinNonlin fits (a two-stage approach), and the %CV columns of
  supplementary Table 1 describe the spread of the individual estimates. They
  are encoded as log-normal IIV, omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2). Their covariance was
  not reported, so the etas are independent. For Kin and Kout this matters:
  each patient's ANC was expressed relative to their own baseline, so their
  individual Kin and Kout must have been strongly correlated, and independent
  etas give simulated individual baselines (Kin/Kout) far more variable than
  in the data. Use typical values, or the PK variability alone, for
  population simulations of the ANC.
* **Baseline.** R(0) is the pre-dose steady state Kin/Kout, the convention of
  the indirect-response model; with the tabulated geometric means this is
  110% rather than 100% of baseline (see the Figure 3a section).
* **Residual error.** Not reported for any model; fixed to zero.
* **Weight.** V/F was reported per kilogram and the dose given per kilogram;
  the model scales V/F linearly with body weight and takes the total dose in
  ug, so CL/F is also proportional to weight. Weight was not tested as a
  covariate in the paper.
* **ALT model not packaged.** The paper also fitted an indirect stimulatory
  model of ALT (dR/dt = Kin [1 + Smax Cp^g / (SC50^g + Cp^g)] - Kout R).
  Only the Hill coefficient (13.5) is reported; Kin, Kout, Smax and SC50 are
  not given anywhere in the article or its supplements, and the authors state
  that the fit was poor and should be treated with caution. It is therefore
  not included.
* **Assay.** The immunoassay measures pegylated and free interferon together;
  concentrations are reported as peginterferon alfa-2b.
* **Literature check.** No erratum or correction was found for this article
  (Europe PMC, checked 2026-11-19).
